briefs.headline: indieMagic to bring a bit of music magic to Mysuru with Easy Wanderlings
briefs.deck: indieMagic, a new concert series, debuts with Pune-origin band Easy Wanderlings this weekend
briefs.bodyText:
After a series of shows at The Heritage House in Mysuru that spanned jazz and global sounds, concert promoter Pranav Bhat felt the combination of live music in a heritage property was a setting that paired quite well in terms of creating an atmosphere.
Bhat, who also runs an art management initiative, recalled there was no dearth of heritage structures in Mysuru and said he always wanted to showcase artistic performances in unique spaces. With the launch of indieMagic, his new concert series in the city, Bhat is one step closer to that dream.
The inaugural edition takes place on September 12 at the century-old heritage venue space Wind Chimes in Nazarbad, Mysuru, and will feature a performance by Pune-origin band Easy Wanderlings as part of their ongoing India tour.
While a lot of support has come forward from city-based companies, Bhat found partners for indieMagic with Resonators by 7 Hills, Wind Chimes and Parabrahma Studios. It helped that Sanjay, owner of Wind Chimes, was a “big supporter of music,” says Bhat.
The entrepreneur also got word to reach Pramoda Devi Wadiyar. Bhat recalls how he attended a concert on August 14 by the Mysuru Music Association featuring the 85-member TOCCATA orchestra from the UK. “I had attended the concert after buying a front-row seat, and it turned out that she was sitting right in front of me,” he says.
Acting on the window of opportunity, he introduced himself and briefly told her about the idea for indieMagic. “She patiently listened to me and graciously offered me the opportunity to present the details of my idea at the royal residence; it was a great honour to do so,” he says.
The concert series plans to take place every three to four months, with future editions slated to include jazz band Derek and The Cats (who will perform at indieMagic in December). The organiser is also in talks with the Vasu Dixit Collective and Swarathma for possible future editions and is dreaming big. “Some of the artistes I’m considering for future editions include Jatayu, Taba Chake, Blackstratblues, Param, Alva Kuuto and maybe, one fine day, even Peter Cat Recording Co,” he says, name-checking big and rising indie acts alike.
It was seeing Easy Wanderlings’ availability to perform as part of their larger tour that set in motion the idea to have them kick off indieMagic. Bhat says he caught a performance of the band in Mumbai and was determined to program them for whenever he did a show in Mysuru. “The stars somehow just found a way to align themselves. One day, I got a call from Sanyanth Naroth, founder and songwriter of Easy Wanderlings saying, ‘We are doing our 10-year anniversary tour and will be hitting The Humming Tree in Bengaluru on September 11. Let us do something in Mysuru around that time.’ I took it as the perfect opportunity to launch indieMagic,” he adds.
Within minutes, early bird tickets for the show sold out, thanks to word spreading about the band’s performance in Mysuru. The shows in Mysuru and Bengaluru form the middle of Easy Wanderlings’ ongoing Ten Years on the Map India tour, which kicked off in New Delhi in August and is slated to close in Ahmedabad in October.
“Over the last 10 years, our songs have travelled far beyond us,” says founder and songwriter Sanyanth Naroth. “They have been the accompanying track on road trips, offered comfort on lonely days, become part of weddings, and quietly found a place in people’s lives. This tour is our way of bringing those songs back to spaces where people can truly listen, connect, and share an evening together.”
In the age of concerts often driven by experiences that take away from the music, Bhat hopes that indieMagic can provide something more wholesome. He belives accessibility across ages is also key to the concert series thriving, where young listeners, families and everyone in between feels welcomed.
“Just regular people who are curious about good music,” he says. It is one thing to start a new concert series for independent music, but it is another matter to sustain it. Bhat is confident on that front as well. “I truly believe that it is the organiser or curator’s job to promote the music in the right manner and gather an audience around the artiste’s music. Once I am confident that an artiste can perform and deliver, I do everything in my capacity to gather the crowd they deserve.”
Easy Wanderlings perform at The Humming Tree, Bengaluru on September 11 and as part of indieMagic at Wind Chimes, Mysuru on September 12. Tickets on SkillBoxes and District

briefs.headline: Green buildings, old wages: Bengaluru construction workers yet to benefit from low-carbon push
briefs.deck: The findings are based on focus group discussions with 55 construction workers and interviews with 15 stakeholders in Bengaluru, along with a review of existing research
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru’s push for greener buildings may create a new set of jobs, but for the workers already building the city, the transition has so far meant little change in their wages or working conditions.
A new study has found that an unskilled construction worker on a large, code-compliant project in Bengaluru can earn as little as ₹500 a day, below the State’s mandated minimum wage of ₹669.61, while workers on smaller projects earn between ₹700 and ₹1,000 a day, according to a WRI India working paper.
The study found no wage difference between workers employed on low-carbon certified buildings and those working on conventional projects.
The working paper, Decent green jobs as a pathway for fair urban transitions -- A study of Bengaluru’s buildings sector, examines what the shift to low-carbon construction could mean for the city’s construction workforce, and that buildings account for more than half of Bengaluru’s greenhouse gas emissions, making the sector a major focus of the city’s climate action plans.
The findings are based on focus group discussions with 55 construction workers and interviews with 15 stakeholders in Bengaluru, along with a review of existing research. The study was undertaken by a group of authors, including Sajad S. Santhosh, Shrimoyee Bhattacharya, and Kiran Shaila Ramesh from WRI India.
The study points that new employment could emerge in areas such as retrofitting old buildings, and managing construction and demolition waste, and that existing workers such as masons, carpenters and electricians could move into green jobs by learning to work with low-carbon materials, designs and construction techniques.
However, the paper argues that merely creating these jobs will not ensure that workers benefit from the transition.
Construction attracts migrant workers because it generally pays more than agriculture. However, migrant workers often struggle to access their legal entitlements, including benefits available through the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, the paper observed.
It found differences between large and small construction projects. Large projects, which are more likely to comply with building codes, are expected to generate greater demand for specialised green jobs. Workers on large projects generally have safer working conditions and more days of employment, while smaller projects tend to offer slightly higher daily wages.
However, the working paper found no significant difference in working conditions between low-carbon and conventional building projects as safety practices are not uniformly enforced, and existing safety norms do not adequately address the environmental stress faced by workers, including exposure to extreme heat.
Highlighting the observations, the researchers called for better mechanisms to help workers access welfare benefits and for labour welfare to be incorporated into policies aimed at reducing emissions from buildings. The study argues that this could allow Bengaluru to tackle two problems at the same time — cut emissions from its buildings while making the workers who build them less vulnerable.

briefs.headline: In Bengaluru, many waste collectors not paid for four months
briefs.deck: This comes even as Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda recently pointed out absenteeism among pourakarmikas who sweep the streets, drawing the ire of both pourakarmikas and waste collectors, who have demanded an apology
briefs.bodyText:
Many of Bengaluru’s waste collectors are again struggling as they have not been paid salaries for several months. While their salaries have remained irregular and the contractors usually pay them once every two months, this time, in many areas, they haven’t gotten their salaries for nearly four months, making it difficult to make ends meet.
This comes even as Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda recently pointed out absenteeism among pourakarmikas who sweep the streets, drawing the ire of both pourakarmikas and waste collectors, who have demanded an apology.
“It is easy to pull up solid waste workers, who are one of the most vulnerable. But has the civic body fulfilled its responsibility towards them in the first place?” asked Appanna, of BBMP Pourakarmikara Sangha.
Irregular payments
Chinnappa, a waste collector in East Bengaluru, said that they are forced to make a life out of what residents give them informally, ragpicking, selling plastic and other dry waste. “Imagine having to run the house with only this kind of uncertainty. I have been working as a driver for six years now. This has always been the case,” he said. He hasn’t gotten his salary for over three months.
A few others are lucky. Ramesh, another garbage vehicle driver, said that his contractors paid salaries for two months 15 days ago. He expressed hope for regular pay every month, adding, “My wife works as a construction labourer and we live on her earnings.”
Contractors blame civic body
Garbage management contractor Balasubramanyam alleged that red tape and several other factors had led to irregular and delayed payments. “The last time our bills were cleared was in March 2026. But contractors are trying to give salaries to our workers, many times through debt,” he said.
Karee Gowda, CEO, Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd (BSWML), was not available for comment.
Workers targeted
Mr. Appanna said workers who were demanding salaries on time were being targeted by contractors. “Such workers are usually fired from their jobs. They are replaced by migrants, who are even more vulnerable. Most of them live in tin sheds and any assertion by them is countered with threats of being branded illegal immigrants or evicted from the lands they stay on. The civic body mandates these workers must get ₹21,000 a month. The local workers get around ₹13,000, but the migrants are paid less than ₹10,000 and exploited even further,” he said.

stories.headline: Small towns power Quick-commerce biz for Flipkart
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Small towns are fueling the growth of Flipkart’s quick commerce business Minutes. Cities such as Siliguri, Ambala, Barabanki, Bhagalpur and Durgapur are seeing huge consumer adoption with the overall customer base growing nearly 25 times year-on-year across such regions, the Walmart-owned company said.
The broader Minutes business has expanded four times y-o-y since its launch two years back. Minutes has now widened its footprint to nearly 1,200 dark stores covering more than 150 cities. In a statement, Flipkart said that around 60% of customers return to shop on Minutes. The instant delivery business rivals Amazon’s Now, Eternal’s Blinkit, Swiggy’s Instamart and Zepto.
In an interaction, Kunal Gupta, Senior Vice President and Head of Flipkart Minutes said that demand on the platform has grown beyond everyday essentials with consumers also shopping for gourmet and premium products. Gourmet and specialty grocery, launched within the past year, has grown eight times, led by demand for cold-pressed oils, imported cheeses, international avocado varieties and Korean ready-to-eat meals. In fact, consumers are adding products such as Korean noodles, sauces and ready-to-eat meals, alongside premium skincare and personal care categories even in smaller cities.
Flipkart is understood to be piloting a standalone app for Minutes with a wider rollout is expected ahead of its annual festive sales in October. 
“We believe a standalone app would help create a sharper identity for Minutes as a QC platform rather than keeping it embedded within Flipkart’s broader e-commerce proposition. The timing also appears favourable, with the wider rollout planned ahead of BBD (Big Billion Days), a period of significantly higher consumer traffic and engagement for Flipkart – which would provide an opportunity to drive initial discovery and awareness of the Minutes app,” analysts at JM Financial said in a note.
Among consumer cohorts, Gen Z has emerged as the fastest-growing customer cohort on Minutes, with the customer base growing nearly five times y-o-y in the past twelve months. Gen Z drives over 45% of orders across categories such as beauty, electronics, gaming, wearables, fragrance, health and nutrition, and grooming, the firm said.
"In two years, Flipkart Minutes has evolved from a convenience offering into a broader shopping channel, with customers using it for much more than their daily essentials. What is particularly interesting is how quickly this behaviour is spreading beyond the largest cities, while Gen Z is also bringing new categories and new shopping occasions to the platform. With our growing network, we have an opportunity to make this experience available to more consumers across the country, while creating new opportunities for brands, farmers and local businesses to reach customers,” Gupta said.

stories.headline: Gross SIP flows, fund industry assets at record high
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Discounting volatility in the stock market, investors poured in money through the mutual fund route that led to a record Rs 32,297 crore in gross monthly inflows through the systematic investment plan (SIP) route in Aug. This, combined with strong buying across most equity mutual fund categories, lifted the total assets managed by the fund industry to just a tad above the Rs 87 lakh crore mark, also a new all-time high level, data from industry trade body AMFI showed.
According to Navneet Munot, MD & CEO of HDFC AMC, in Aug, the fund industry extended a trend that has been observed for some time now as SIP inflows climbed to a record high even as the market remained volatile on global cues.
AMFI data showed that as of Aug 31, SIP assets stood at Rs 18.6 lakh crore, up 2.8% on the month, while the number of contributing SIP accounts was at a little over 10 crore.
During the month, net inflows into equity schemes were Rs 29,329 crore. This was the 66th consecutive month of net inflows through this fund category. Among equity fund categories, while small-cap funds took in a net Rs 7,973 crore, mid-cap schemes recorded net inflows worth Rs 6,989 crore, and flexicap funds Rs 5,059 crore.
AMFI data also showed that in Aug, retail folios (equity + hybrid + solutions-oriented schemes) were at 21.6 crore, up from 21.4 crore the previous month.
According to Saugata Chatterjee, president & deputy CEO, Nippon India Mutual Fund, the continued growth in industry folios was the most encouraging takeaway from Aug data that reflected the widening reach of mutual funds. "Record-high SIP contributions, along with a moderating stoppage ratio, further demonstrate the growing discipline of Indian investors. The continued preference for small-cap and mid-cap funds indicates investors' desire to participate in the broader opportunity across corporate India. Given the nature of these segments, disciplined allocation, patience and a longer investment horizon remain important."

stories.headline: Growth spurt: On data by Federation of Automobile Dealers’ Associations
stories.deck: Alternative powertrains are now mainstream in automobiles
stories.bodyText:
According to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers’ Associations (FADA), total vehicle registrations in August have increased 17.5% year on year, recording the all-time highest volume for the month, and with alternative powertrains, i.e., CNG, electric, and hybrids, leading passenger vehicle sales for the first time. But upon a closer look, some confounding factors emerge that also warrant caution about the figures. First, July 2026 itself was a strong month, with the August numbers 6.4% lower, possibly due to the monsoon. Second, the number of vehicles retailed in rural areas grew 19.7% year on year over 15.1% in urban areas; passenger vehicles sales likewise increased 24.9% in rural areas versus 10.9% in urban areas. This could be due to rising disposable incomes and consistent state capital expenditure on semi-urban infrastructure. However, tractor sales have in the past indicated monsoon-related rural stress, and while their sales are virtually unchanged year on year, they declined 25% month on month. Together with two-wheelers and passenger vehicles selling well, the trend suggests that non-farm rural incomes and mobility could be strengthening more than capital spending linked to agriculture. Third, last year, the GST Council reduced taxes on small cars, motorcycles (up to 350 cc), three-wheelers, buses, and goods vehicles, so August 2025 sales growth dropped as buyers waited for the new rates from September. Fourth, while CNG, hybrid, and electric powertrains beat petrol/ethanol vehicle sales by 1.1 percentage points, most hybrid vehicles still burn petrol while CNG itself is a fossil fuel. So the lead taken by alternative powertrains is not synonymous with a lead of non-fossil-fuel vehicles.
That said, petrol vehicles falling behind is still notable; the data also show that between August 2024 and August 2026, CNG and electric powertrains contributed most of the surge, implying that Indians are switching to alternatives that are cheaper to run, in light of the West Asia conflict and, to a lesser degree, concerns over ethanol blending. Next, the move away from petrol is uneven: three-wheelers are predominantly electric while two-wheelers catch up, and passenger cars’ powertrains continue to diversify. And electrification continues to reflect rising consumer demand as much as industrial policy. Finally, FADA also reported that, despite record sales, dealers are holding 38-40 days of inventory against the recommended 21. So while the petrol era is far from over, the Indian automotive industry has commenced the mass-market integration of alternative powertrains. But that said, only if September-November preserves the gains in alternative powertrains after the base effect disappears, and dealer inventories return to normal levels, can August 2026 be considered a historic moment.

stories.headline: Opportunities high for Indian foundries to supply global players, say experts

Indian manufacturers have huge potential to tap into the global market as more businesses are looking at suppliers and opportunities in India, said Parag Sharma, vice-president of Global Purchasing and Supply Chain, India and Asia Pacific Region, Stellantis.

briefs.headline: Emerging sectors to drive next industrial revolution: Report
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Emerging sectors, such as space, data centers, solar energy, semiconductors and electronics are set to drive the next phase of industrial revolution in India as the large domestic opportunity is driving private participation.
Supportive govt policies, such as tax holidays for establishing data centres, large incentive schemes for boosting semiconductor production, electronics and solar cells, along with promoting greater private participation in the space sector, are some of the policies that will drive growth in these industries, a report by global investment banker Jefferies has said.
The report said India's next industrial revolution is being built on an already significant manufacturing base in select industries, such as steel, cement, automobiles and oil refineries. "The combination of scale, domestic demand, manufacturing capabilities and policy support provides a strong foundation for the country's next growth engines in (these industries)," the report said.
In the space sector, the report noted that India is among a handful of spacefaring nations with "global competitive capabilities" and govt is targeting nearly five times expansion in the space economy to $40-50 billion over 2023-30. 
From just one space startup in 2014 to over 400 in 2026, investor interest is rising with cumulative private investment reaching $600 million by 2025-26. "Indian space start-ups are now progressing from early stage innovation to commercial execution."
In semiconductors, the report said India's aspirations are moving from policy intent to execution with nearly $20 billion of investments, including a chip fab under construction. A new $13 billion incentive plan should further expand the ecosystem and boost value addition, including chip design.
Regarding data centres, the report said the space is rapidly emerging as a strategic digital infrastructure segment, with colocation capacity expanding five times over the past five years to 2 GW (gigawatt). "Capacity is expected to grow another five times to nearly 10GW over the next five years, supported by favourable cost economics, policy support and rising hyperscale demand."

briefs.headline: Apple's foldable debut to lift mkt, test Samsung
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Apple could bring more buyers to foldables without winning most of them. Foldable phones have flexible screens that let them open into larger displays or fold into more compact devices. The Cupertino-based company's entry with the iPhone Duo is expected to draw attention to a smartphone category that remains small in India, while Samsung's wider price range could help it capture much of the increase in sales.
At Rs 2,99,900, the Duo gives iPhone users a foldable within Apple's ecosystem. Its immediate contribution, however, could be greater in consumer awareness, developer interest and market value than in shipment volumes.
"Samsung has been building this category for years, and its pricing spread across multiple foldable form factors only strengthens that position for now," said Upasana Joshi of IDC India.
India's foldable shipments stood at just under 6.3 lakh units in 2025, against total smartphone shipments of 15.2 crore, according to IDC. Samsung accounted for the vast majority. IDC expects foldable shipments to reach 8-8.5 lakh units in 2026, even as overall smartphone shipments decline to around 12.5 crore. 
Joshi said Apple's pricing would keep the Duo largely within the super-premium segment initially, limiting the volumes it could generate to challenge Samsung's leadership.
Counterpoint Research's Tarun Pathak expects India's foldable market to cross 10 lakh units next year, with Samsung driving much of that expansion because of its price advantage. Apple could encourage developers to build better experiences and help consumers understand the category.
"The bigger message is that foldables are moving beyond being just a technology showcase and becoming a more established premium smartphone category," Pathak said. India has an installed base of around 30 lakh foldables against more than 74 crore smartphone users, according to Pathak. He does not expect the category to become mass market for another three-to-four years.
For Apple, the commercial opportunity extends beyond unit sales. Prabhu Ram of CyberMedia Research described the Duo as "a halo offering to elevate overall portfolio ASPs", positioning it above the flagship lineup for affluent buyers. Apple's entry could reinforce shift towards wider, book-style foldables, which Pathak said offer a more natural tablet-like experience for documents, video and multitasking.

briefs.headline: 'Building tomorrow's market today with tokenised bonds'
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: 
RBI
 governor Sanjay Malhotra said early experiments with financial asset tokenisation were helping the regulator test the infrastructure for future markets as he launched a pilot enabling instant settlement of tokenised corporate bonds through the eRupee.
Malhotra on Thursday launched the Demat 2.0 pilot with Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey at the Global Fintech Fest. The initiative enables corporate bonds to be tokenised and settled through the central bank digital currency, while automating coupon payments and redemption.
RBI is also looking to expand the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) as common digital rails for consent-based credit delivery. It plans to roll out the proposed Digital Payments Intelligence Platform alongside MuleHunter.ai to strengthen real-time fraud mitigation. The central bank is continuing programmable CBDC pilots for targeted govt benefit transfers, including PMGKAY, while expanding the wholesale CBDC market architecture.
He said AI, quantum computing and tokenisation should be applied to practical problems such as improving consumer services, addressing credit gaps, increasing operational efficiency and reducing fraud. At the same time, firms need to address risks from algorithmic opacity, bias, financial exclusion, herding behaviour, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, data privacy and the erosion of human judgement in AI-based decision-making.
The governor also stressed that customer data should be treated as a fiduciary responsibility, with its use bound by purpose and consent rather than treated as an asset to be monetised.

briefs.headline: Bahrain court has ruled in our favour in bond case: HDFC
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Bahrain's high civil court rejected all seven legal proceedings filed against HDFC Bank by investors over Credit Suisse Additional Tier 1 (CS AT1) bonds, with the latest two cases dismissed on Sept 9, the bank said on Thursday. Five similar cases were rejected by the court between July and Aug.
AT1 bonds are risky instruments where investors lose money if the issuing bank's net worth is wiped out. The seven investors had alleged gross negligence, intentional misrepresentation, incorrect customer classification, non-disclosure of product features, misuse of financial leverage and breach of suitability principles. The court rejected the claims after finding that the investors had failed to produce sufficient admissible evidence to substantiate the allegations or establish losses caused by the bank.

briefs.headline: May tweak F&O settlement price mechanism: Sebi chief
briefs.deck: Pandey Reiterates There Is No Going Back On CAS System
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Thursday said that the newly introduced Closing Auction Session (CAS) will stay but the regulator is studying if the mechanism to arrive at derivatives settlement prices could be changed. Pandey also said that MSCI, one of the largest index service providers in the world, has acknowledged that even though the overlapping of CAS and the index's rebalancing window coincided on Aug 31, the process had ended without any glitch.
CAS, a new system of determining the end-of-the-day price for stocks, was introduced on Aug 3 but faced severe criticism for bringing in extreme volatility in the market, including substantial closing price differential on the two exchanges, BSE and NSE.
In Thursday's session, as sensex's weekly derivatives contracts were to expire, the index witnessed swings of over 1,000 points. Earlier, on Aug 27, as weekly and monthly contracts on sensex expired, the index and bankex had both witnessed wild swings within minutes of the day's closing.
After resisting a change to the CAS system, last week, Sebi said that it would review the existing mechanism and would soon come out with a consultation paper for the same. 
Currently, CAS is allowed only in those stocks that are also traded in the futures & options (F&O) segments of the bourses. For the rest of the stocks, the earlier mechanism of volume-weighted average price (V-WAP) is followed.
On Thursday, Pandey also said that the rollout of CAS across several developed markets had faced teething troubles, including liquidity in the market. He, however, added that several market participants have praised CAS.
Earlier, while delivering a speech at the Global Fintech Festival, the Sebi chief said that in the age of agentic AI, tokenisation, quantum computing and other advancements in the technology space, a key question for regulators was how to make "innovation scalable without making risk scalable at the same pace." That was the challenge of "growing fast, growing safe", he said.
Pandey also said that as market participants use advanced technologies at greater speed and scale, regulators must be able to supervise with comparable sophistication.
"This is where SupTech offers tremendous opportunity. The objective is not simply to automate supervision, but to use data, analytics and AI to identify patterns that may not be visible through traditional methods. At Sebi, we are moving in this direction, with the aim of making supervision increasingly predictive and capable of identifying emerging risks early," he said.

briefs.headline: Shopping online? From January, you'll see the discount margin
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: From Jan, e-commerce entities will have to display both the "reduced price" and "prior price" whenever they announce a price cut, including during festive sale seasons. The "prior price" will be the lowest price at which the product was offered up to 30 days before the announcement of discount.
The provision is part of the sweeping amendments to Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules notified by the consumer affairs department on Thursday to tighten norms on price transparency, sponsored listings, search-result manipulation and dark patterns.
Officials said the move is aimed at bringing greater transparency to online pricing. If consumers find discrepancies in the prices displayed by e-commerce platforms, they can lodge complaints with National Consumer Helpline (NCH).
Under the amended rules, every e-commerce entity must be integrated with NCH convergence mechanism. The provision has been introduced as nearly 29% of the 17.7 lakh complaints received by the helpline in 2025 were related to the e-commerce sector. Platforms will also be required to provide complainants with a copy of the complaint as recorded by their grievance officer.
The rules also prohibit e-commerce entities from manipulating search results in a manner that misleads users or affects the relevance of results to a consumer's search query. Sponsored listings must now carry "clear and prominent disclosures" so that consumers can distinguish paid promotions from organic search results.

stories.headline: Sabalenka storms past Pegula, closes in on historic US Open three-peat
stories.deck: Aryna Sabalenka marches towards a remarkable U.S. Open hat-trick, having conquered Jessica Pegula in the semifinals. Demonstrating sheer dominance, she clinched the second set with ease. Now, Sabalenka eyes her opponent for the final, either Elena Rybakina or Coco Gauff. A win on Saturday would see her become the first since Serena Williams to claim three consecutive titles, extending her U.S.…
stories.bodyText:
Aryna Sabalenka is one win away from a historic U.S. Open hat-trick after the top seed powered past Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2 in the semifinal on Thursday night.
For much of the opening set, there was little to separate the two players. But once Sabalenka found her opening, the match changed dramatically. She began attacking Pegula's second serve with greater aggression and carried that momentum into a dominant second set, producing some of her best tennis of the tournament.
“No complaints,” Sabalenka said. “I’m just super happy that I was able to pull out such tennis.”
The Belarusian will play either No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina or No. 4 Coco Gauff in Saturday's final. A victory would make Sabalenka the first player since Serena Williams in 2012-14 to win three consecutive U.S. Open titles.
Sabalenka is also set to surrender the No. 1 ranking to Rybakina next week, ending her run of 99 consecutive weeks at the top. But she has made it clear that another trophy in New York would make giving up the ranking far easier to accept.
And based on the way she dismantled Pegula, Sabalenka will enter Saturday's final with plenty of belief.
Sabalenka turns a tight contest into a one-sided finish
The semifinal initially followed the pattern of Sabalenka's previous two meetings with Pegula at the business end of the U.S. Open. Their 2024 final and 2025 semifinal were both closely fought for long periods, but this time Sabalenka eventually found another gear.
She finished with 29 winners compared with Pegula's 12 and dominated the American on second-serve points, winning 14 of 19.
“I was so desperate for the win, I wanted it badly,” Sabalenka said.
The victory extended Sabalenka's winning streak at the U.S. Open to 19 matches. She has not lost at Flushing Meadows since Gauff defeated her in the 2023 final.
The result also maintained the dominance of the tournament's top four seeds. For the first time since 1975, all four women's semifinalists came from the top four positions in the draw.
Sabalenka, Rybakina and Gauff have already collected multiple major titles, while Pegula continues to chase the first Grand Slam trophy of her career.
Pegula hangs on before Sabalenka finds the breakthrough
Pegula, a Buffalo, New York native, had hoped her strongest surface and favourite Grand Slam would finally provide the setting for a maiden major title.
She managed to stay with Sabalenka early on. The score was 4-4 after only 25 minutes, while Sabalenka began to show signs of frustration as she struggled to make an impact on Pegula's serve.
After one error, the No. 1 seed turned towards her coaches' box in visible disgust.
Pegula had won 18 of 20 points on her first serve when she came out to serve at 5-6. But that was where Sabalenka finally broke the deadlock.
A backhand winner gave her the first opening. Pegula then pushed a forehand long before Sabalenka produced another winner to earn set point. She closed out the set two points later, turning a finely balanced contest on its head.
The hard courts that suit Pegula also happen to provide the perfect stage for Sabalenka's power game, and the Belarusian began making that difference count.
Pegula has no answer as Sabalenka takes control
Sabalenka struck again in Pegula's second service game of the second set. She eventually pounced on a 77 mph second serve, driving a forehand back at 90 mph. Pegula could not recover in time, and Sabalenka moved ahead 3-1.
It was exactly the kind of pressure Sabalenka had said she enjoyed facing against Pegula.
The American entered the semifinal having recorded the most wins on tour this season, while also sharing the lead for hard-court victories. Sabalenka had described her as the kind of opponent who could test her and force her to respond whenever she was put under pressure.
On Thursday, Sabalenka supplied those answers repeatedly.
Pegula's frustration boiled over late in the match. After Sabalenka produced a powerful low passing shot that Pegula could only volley into the net, the No. 3 seed threw her racket onto the court.

stories.headline: HC denies Vinesh Phogat entry to Worlds trials: ‘Not inclined to grant exemption’
stories.deck: The Delhi High Court has denied Vinesh Phogat an interim exemption to participate in the selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Championships. The court emphasised the need for uniform eligibility criteria applicable to all athletes. Although Phogat's maternity challenges will be assessed in terms of policy validity, the court has ruled against granting interim relief, thus barring her…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The 
Delhi High Court
 on Thursday refused to allow wrestler 
Vinesh Phogat
 to participate in the women’s selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Championships, declining her request for an interim exemption from the eligibility criteria prescribed by the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI).
Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma, in a late-night interim order, said that at this stage, the court was not inclined to grant an interim exemption from the eligibility criteria to allow Phogat to participate in the selection trials on September 14.
“To reiterate, the criteria prescribed under the circular dated September 7, 2026 apply uniformly to all athletes. An athlete who has not participated in the prescribed competitions, for whatever reason, would not fall within the eligibility categories specified by respondent no. 1 (WFI),” the court said.
The high court passed the order while dismissing an application by Phogat, who has returned from maternity leave, seeking permission to participate in the women’s selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Championships.
Court flags Phogat’s maternity circumstances
The court said Phogat’s circumstances relating to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum recovery would require consideration while examining the validity of the policy. 
However, that does not, at the interim stage, by itself entitle her to a direction permitting her to participate contrary to the eligibility criteria, it added.
“Granting such interim relief to the petitioner alone, without first adjudicating upon the policy itself, may consequently result in unequal treatment of similarly situated athletes who are not before this court,” it said.
The court added that without expressing any final opinion on the validity of the circular or on the merits of the pending disciplinary proceedings, it was not inclined to grant the interim relief.
Phogat challenges September 7 WFI circular
Phogat, in her application filed in a pending petition, had also sought a stay on the operation of a September 7 circular issued by the WFI prescribing the eligibility criteria for the selection trials scheduled for September 14 at the Indira Gandhi Stadium here.
The fresh application was filed in the main petition in which Phogat has sought formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave.
In the application, she sought a stay on the circular as it excludes her from participating in the selection trials for the championship scheduled to be held at Astana, Kazakhstan from October 24 to November 1.
The WFI circular provides for women’s trials in six Olympic weight categories. Phogat contended that the latest selection framework creates a closed pathway by making eligibility dependent on participation and performance in specified qualifying competitions.
The plea said the circular places Phogat in a position where she is excluded not because she has been assessed and found wanting on sporting merit but because she was unable to participate in the particular competitions selected by WFI as gateways to the present selection trials.
Court had sought WFI, Centre response
It said the framework contains no mechanism to account for an athlete who was unable to participate in the prescribed competitions for maternity-related reasons.
On September 1, the high court sought the response of WFI and the Centre on Phogat’s plea seeking formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave.
In the petition, she has sought directions for formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning from maternity, transparent and objectively verifiable selection and nomination processes, and an alternative mechanism for athletes disadvantaged by maternity-related absence.
Phogat, who became a mother in July 2025, said upon resuming her wrestling career after childbirth, she was made to re-enter the competitive pathway without any accommodation for the period she was unable to compete due to maternity.
The wrestler has also filed another petition seeking quashing of two show cause notices issued to her by the WFI and disciplinary proceedings initiated against her.
WFI’s counsel had said they kept the hearing twice but “there has been no show”; a final opportunity was given and the hearing was on September 2.
In the plea, Phogat said that the two notices issued to her on May 9 and June 17 were part of a continuing pattern of arbitrary and mala fide action by the WFI, obstructing her return to competitive wrestling after maternity.

stories.headline: Shafali steers India to Women’s Asia Cup final
stories.deck: With seven titles (four in 50-over and three T20s), India are the most successful team in the tournament
stories.bodyText:
Shafali Verma lived a charmed life for her stroke filled 64 off 40 balls as India marched into yet another Women's Asia Cup final with a comfortable 40-run win over Bangladesh here on Thursday.
On a slow surface where batting was a struggle for majority of the batters, Shafali stood out with her fluent effort to take India to 149 for six. The Indian opener was dropped as many as three times and she duly made Bangladesh pay for those mistakes.
Considering the conditions and India's bowling resources, the seven-time champions were expected to defend the target and they did rather comfortably, limiting Bangladesh to 109 for 7 in 20 overs.
Bangladesh never threatened India despite the aggressive intent of opener Juairiya Ferdous (14 off 18). Eventually Ferdous and her opening partner Dilara Akter (21 off 26) fell while attempting to clear the mid-wicket boundary. Kranti Gaud's running catch to get ride of Akter was a brilliant effort on an otherwise ordinary day for the fielders.
Like the last game, Pratika Rawal dropped a couple of catches. The Indian spin trio of Deepti Sharma (3/26), Shree Charani (1/14) and Prema Rawat (1/21) too delivered in spin friendly conditions.
It has been a low scoring tournament mainly due to the slow nature of the pitches here. Considering that and Bangaldesh's batting, India knew deep down they had got enough on the board. They will play with either Pakistan or Sri Lanka in the final scheduled for Sunday.
With seven titles (four in 50-over and three T20s), India are the most successful team in the tournament. They had a suffered a shocking loss to Sri Lanka in the previous edition.
Earlier, the Bangladesh bowling attack, which has been impressive in the tournament, was able to keep the accomplished Indian batters quiet for majority of the innings.
In total, four dropped catches let Bangladesh down else India would have struggled to get past the 120-run mark.
India captain Harmanpreet Kaur (24 not out off 28), usually a good player of spin, struggled for majority of her innings only managing four runs off her first 16 balls.
Shafali single-handedly steered India to a competitive total notwithstanding her remarkable stroke of luck, having been dropped on 6, 11 and 56. While the batters in the top four batted at a sub 100 strike rate, Shafali ended with an impressive strike rate of 160 that included three sixes off the spinners.
The destructive opener played her shots all around the park and her innings included a front foot pull off pacer Marufa Akter, reverse sweep and massive hits down the ground off the spinners. India did well to reach 45 for one in the powerplay but could not accelerate in the middle overs.
India's new number three Pratika Rawal (20 off 24) has been under pressure in the tournament but on Thursday she made a sizzling start, a copy book cover drive off Akter. Later in her innings, she came out of the crease to hit a six before falling to the same bowler.
Richa Ghosh (21 off 16) too was slow to get off the blocks but managed to add valuable runs. Skipper Harmanpreet redeemed herself with a couple of sixes towards the end.

briefs.headline: 'Gukesh not in a position to defend': Carlsen on Championship clash vs Sindarov
briefs.deck: Magnus Carlsen says Gukesh should not view his upcoming World Championship match against Javokhir Sindarov as a title defence, but as an opportunity to gain. Carlsen believes Gukesh’s peak level matches or exceeds Sindarov’s, though early momentum will be crucial. He also highlights chess’s psychological nature, suggesting confidence and pressure could significantly influence the short match
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Five-time world champion 
Magnus Carlsen
 has pushed back against the framing of D Gukesh's upcoming World Championship match as a "title defence", arguing that the Indian should instead be approaching it as an opportunity to gain rather than something to protect.
Speaking to the reporters on the sidelines of the Global Chess League (GCL) on Thursday, Carlsen said the way Gukesh has played over the past two years means he shouldn't see himself as merely holding onto what he already has.
"The word 'defend' is really not a good place to begin, because in terms of how Gukesh has played for the last couple of years, he should not be in a position where he has to defend anything," Carlsen said. "He should be in a position where he has everything to gain."
The Norwegian pointed to Gukesh's 2024 form as evidence of his ceiling.
"He has shown previously in 2024 that when things click, he has the potential to play at an extremely high level," Carlsen remarked, adding that while public confidence in a repeat performance may be low, that only sharpens the challenge in front of him. "I don't think a lot of people believe that he will do it now, but I think it's even more of an interesting challenge for him to try and get back to that."
Carlsen was also blunt about the psychological dimension of the contest, suggesting the mental battle could prove just as decisive as anything on the board.
"Chess is a highly psychological game, so it probably won't take a lot to potentially place some doubts in Sindarov's mind and some confidence for Gukesh," he said.
Asked whether Gukesh's current form would matter once the match got underway, Carlsen, who is currently playing for the APL Pipers in the fourth season of GCL, was candid about his broader scepticism of the classical World Championship format itself, calling it a poor mechanism for identifying the strongest player.
"One of the reasons why I believe it's an extraordinarily bad way to determine the best player in the world is that you play classical, which is the most egalitarian format, and you don't play a ton of games as well," he explained. Even a heavily lopsided pre-match assessment, he said, rarely translates into a lopsided scoreline.
"If you think a certain match is 80-20 before it starts, the likelihood is still very high that it's going to be a close score, because chess is such a drawish game."
On the matchup itself, Carlsen was unequivocal that Gukesh holds his own against Sindarov in pure quality.
"Gukesh has shown that his ceiling is on par or better than Sindarov," he added. But given the short format, he warned that early momentum could decide everything.
"If Sindarov is ahead early on, it's probably very, very bad news for Gukesh. If Gukesh is ahead early on, he automatically becomes a significant favourite. That's how these matches work."

briefs.headline: Shafali stars with 64, Deepti strikes thrice as India storm into 10th Asia Cup final
briefs.deck: India secured a dominant 40-run victory over Bangladesh to advance into the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final. Shafali Varma's explosive 64-run innings provided a strong foundation for India's competitive total. India's bowlers applied sustained pressure, restricting Bangladesh to 109 runs in their chase. Deepti Sharma was instrumental with the ball, claiming crucial wickets throughout the match. This…
briefs.bodyText:
India produced another dominant performance with bat and ball to beat Bangladesh by 40 runs and storm into the final of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Thursday. After posting 149/6 in their 20 overs, India’s bowlers delivered under pressure to restrict Bangladesh to 109/7, successfully defending what initially appeared to be a modest total on a slow pitch.
The victory extended India’s unbeaten run in the tournament and secured their place in a 10th successive Women’s Asia Cup final. They will face the winner of the second semi-final between defending champions Sri Lanka and Pakistan in the title clash on September 13.
Shafali’s blazing 64 lifts India
Bangladesh won the toss and opted to field, but Shafali Varma made the most of the opportunity to put India on the front foot.
The explosive opener smashed 64 off 40 balls, hitting seven fours and three sixes, as she held India’s innings together after vice-captain Smriti Mandhana fell for just two. Shafali rode her luck after being dropped three times but made Bangladesh pay with an attacking knock that gave India a competitive total.
Captain 
Harmanpreet Kaur
 struggled for fluency but contributed 24 off 28 balls, including two sixes, while Richa Ghosh added an important 21 off 16 deliveries. Deepti Sharma then provided the late impetus with a quick 13 off six balls, helping India finish just short of 150.
Deepti spins Bangladesh into trouble
Bangladesh needed 150 to reach the final but struggled to maintain momentum throughout their chase. Deepti Sharma once again proved the difference with the ball, claiming 3/26 in four overs and repeatedly breaking Bangladesh's resistance.
Nandani Sharma also impressed, taking 2/10 from two overs, including the final wicket of the innings. Bangladesh’s top order showed glimpses of resistance, with Dilara Akter scoring 21 off 26 balls and Shorna Akter hitting a brisk 22 off 18. But the batting line-up failed to absorb India's sustained pressure.
The Tigresses lost wickets at regular intervals as India tightened their grip on the chase. With the required rate climbing, Bangladesh could only reach 109/7 in 20 overs, falling 40 runs short.
The innings ended in fitting fashion for India, with Nandani Sharma dismissing Rabeya Khan hit-wicket. Khan attempted to slog a slower delivery but ended up dislodging the stumps with her bat while completing the shot.
India eye another Asia Cup title
India’s latest victory keeps their unbeaten campaign intact and sends them into yet another Asia Cup final. The seven-time champions will now await the winner of Sri Lanka vs Pakistan, with the final scheduled for September 13.

briefs.headline: Top names to the fore at the Indian Athletics Final Series
briefs.bodyText:
Even as the biggest names in Indian track and field turned out to test themselves one last time before the Asian Games, hammer thrower Tanya Chaudhary hogged the limelight at the Indian Athletics Final Series on Thursday.
Tanya took gold with a best of 68.35m for a new National record while 18-year-old Anushka Yadav, who became the youngest National record-holder two months back with a 67.02m effort, took silver with 66.34m.
Sadly, there were barely any witnesses to the special occasion as the event was held in the warm-up field of play outside the main ground.
“I was confident because even though it was not officially ratified, I threw beyond 67m at the inter-university games. I have been chasing this record for the last three years, so it feels really good. We have been focusing only on the technical aspects of the throw in training, not as much on power,” Tanya said. “The target now is to go even better and not go below this at the Asian Games. My target for this year was to manage the 70m mark and it is all building towards that.”
The men’s event also witnessed a new National record as Delhi’s Nirbhay Choudhary bettered the decade-old mark of Neeraj Kumar with 71.02m.
On the track, Animesh Kujur sprinted to victory in 10.21 seconds in the 100m ahead of Gurindervir Singh (10.32s) and Rushiprasad Singh (10.33s).
Harita Bhadra, who will represent India in the 200m, took the top spot among women in 11.22s.
“This was my last 100m event for this season and I wanted to do my best, the target now is a medal at the Asian Games,” Harita said.
Animesh completed a 100m-200m double late in the night, winning the latter in 20.59s.
Vishal T.K. expectedly won the packed 400m in 45.36s, followed by Jay Kumar and Manu T.S. Quite interestingly, six of the eight clocked under 46s.
Avinash Sable, returning to steeplechase after almost a year and half, proved he still had no competition, winning more than 18 seconds ahead of second-placed Shubham Bhandare.
The top finishers all received ₹1 lakh prize money.

briefs.headline: Shree Charani creates history at 22, becomes fastest Indian to 50 T20I wickets
briefs.deck: Shree Charani has made history by becoming the fastest Indian bowler to take fifty wickets in women's T20 internationals, completing this achievement in her twenty-ninth T20I appearance. This pivotal moment elevates her status among the world's top bowlers. Furthermore, India's journey in the Asia Cup semifinal has added to the excitement surrounding her performance in international cricket.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Young India spinner Shree Charani etched her name in the record books on Thursday, becoming the fastest Indian bowler to reach 50 wickets in women's T20Is and achieving the milestone at the age of just 22.
Charani reached the landmark in her 29th T20I, putting her joint-second on the all-time list for the fastest bowlers to 50 wickets in the format. China's Mengting Liu holds the outright record, having reached 50 wickets in 28 matches.
New Zealand's Leigh Kasperek and West Indies' Anisa Mohammed also took 29 matches to complete the milestone, putting Charani alongside two established names in the record books.
Fastest to 50 wickets in Women’s T20Is (by matches)
- 28 - Mengting Liu (China)
- 29 - Leigh Kasperek (New Zealand)
- 29 - Anisa Mohammed (West Indies)
- 29 - Shree Charani (India)
- 34 - Sophie Ecclestone (England)
Charani joins elite company
Charani's achievement was even more significant given her age. At 22 years and 37 days, she became the second-youngest Indian to reach 50 women's T20I wickets.
Radha Yadav remains India's youngest to the milestone, having achieved it at 20 years and 334 days. England's Sophie Ecclestone holds the overall record among players from full-member nations, reaching 50 wickets at 20 years and 300 days.
New Zealand's Amelia Kerr, who reached the landmark at 21 years and 354 days, is the third-youngest, while Charani's achievement at 22 years and 37 days puts her fourth on the list.
Youngest to 50 wickets in Women’s T20Is (FM teams)
- 20y 300d - Sophie Ecclestone (ENG)
- 20y 334d - Radha Yadav (IND)
- 21y 354d - Amelia Kerr (NZ)
- 22y 37d - Shree Charani (IND)
- 22y 135d - Stafanie Taylor (WI)
- 22y 187d - Deepti Sharma (IND)
Her landmark wicket came during India's Women's Asia Cup semifinal against Bangladesh at the Dubai International Stadium.
In the sixth over, Charani dismissed Juairiya Ferdous for 14, with wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh completing a catch after the Bangladesh batter attempted to play a big shot against the spinner.
The dismissal was Charani's 50th T20I wicket and came as India looked to defend a competitive total.
India defend 149 after Shafali's blazing fifty
India had posted 149/6 in 20 overs, with Shafali Verma providing the main impetus after the early dismissal of vice-captain Smriti Mandhana for two.
Shafali smashed 64 off 40 balls, hitting seven fours and three sixes, while captain Harmanpreet Kaur remained unbeaten on 24 off 28 balls. Pratika Rawal contributed 20 and Deepti Sharma provided a late burst with 13 off six deliveries.
Richa Ghosh also played a useful cameo, scoring 21 off 16 balls with two sixes.
“It meant a lot because we had to continue. We had been trying to do this for a few matches before as well, but today we managed to do it, and that feels really good,” Richa said during the mid-innings break.
Reflecting on the conditions, she added: “It was slow, and there was some turn, so it's really important.”
With Charani reaching a landmark of her own, India's spin attack received another boost as the seven-time champions looked to book their place in Sunday's final.

briefs.headline: GCL: Alpine Pipers in joint lead despite having a mixed day
briefs.bodyText:
Bibisara Assaubayeva had played seven games and won none. On the eve of her eighth game, her teammate Javokhir Sindarov joked she could take one of his Player-of-the-Match trophies from the Tech Mahindra Global Chess League, as he had many.
Sindarov needn’t be that generous, though Assaubayeva is his girlfriend. She won the award on her own, for her win against Polina Shuvalova, who hadn’t lost a single game in the tournament.
That win by Assaubayeva helped Fyers American Gambits beat Ganges Grandmasters 13-5 in the last match at the Lalit Ashok on Thursday and thus remain in the joint lead with just two rounds remaining in the round-robin league. Sindarov, of course, played his part, winning his game against Ian Nepomniachtchi.
The Grandmasters are still among the leaders though, thanks to a 12-4 victory against the reigning champion Alpine APL Pipers in the day’s opening match. The Pipers, though, bounced back with an 11-6 win against PBG Alaskan Knights.

Cheq Mumba Masters, which scored a crucial 14-5 win against Triveni Continental Kings, has 12 points and is best placed to challenge the three leaders for a place in the final. The Kings remain at the bottom with six points, three less than the Knights.

briefs.headline: Root scripts history, surpasses Smith to become the fielder with most catches in Tests
briefs.deck: On Thursday, Joe Root made history in Test cricket by claiming his 220th catch, overtaking Steve Smith's record. This monumental achievement took place during England's third Test against Pakistan, where they built a commanding lead in the first innings. Meanwhile, Pakistan struggled early in their second innings, facing significant challenges at the crease.
briefs.bodyText:
Joe Root
 scripted a new piece of Test history on Thursday, becoming the most successful fielder in the format after taking his 220th catch during the third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.
Root surpassed Australia’s 
Steve Smith
, who had held the record with 219 catches, to move to the top of the list for most catches by a non-wicketkeeper in Test cricket. The England batter’s latest milestone came at a crucial moment, with the hosts firmly in control of the match.
Root makes 220th catch look easy
The record-breaking catch came in the opening over of Pakistan’s second innings. Ollie Robinson found the edge of Abdullah Shafique’s bat, with the ball travelling low towards Root at first slip. Root reacted quickly, bending down to complete a sharp catch and send Shafique back for a three-ball duck.
Robinson went wide of the crease and angled a good-length delivery into the fifth-stump channel. Shafique attempted to defend while playing inside the line, only to edge the ball towards Root, who made a difficult low catch appear remarkably straightforward.
It was also Robinson’s 21st wicket of the series, adding to Pakistan’s growing problems with the bat.
Most catches as a fielder in Tests
- 220* - Joe Root
- 219 - Steven Smith
- 210 - Rahul Dravid
- 205 - M Jayawardene
- 200 - Jacques Kallis
England take a massive 320-run lead
Root’s record came shortly after England had completed a commanding first-innings performance, being bowled out for 453 to take a massive 320-run lead over Pakistan.
The visitors had been dismissed for just 133 on the opening day and now face one final opportunity to produce a competitive score in the series. Pakistan have failed to cross 200 in any of their first three innings in the Test series, and their second innings could hardly have started worse, with Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique falling in the first over Ollie Robinson giving England an immediate advantage.

briefs.headline: Manav-Manush pair hopes to make amends
briefs.deck: The narrow loss at the Hangzhou Asiad still rankles the duo; the Gujarat paddlers are India’s best bet for a medal at the continental extravaganza
briefs.bodyText:
India’s World No. 3 men’s doubles pair of Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah will head into the Asian Games as the country’s strongest table tennis medal prospects, carrying with them the lingering disappointment of a near-miss in Hangzhou three years ago.
The Gujarat duo had come within a point of a medal in Hangzhou, before losing a tense quarterfinal to South Korea’s Jang Woo-jin and Lim Jong-hoon, the then World No. 1 pair.
The defeat, Manush admitted, continues to rankle.
“It’s at the back of the mind. I think the wounds of the last Asian Games haven’t healed yet. Me and Manav both always speak about that match. We want to recover from that loss,” Manush told The Hindu.
The Indians had a match point against the Korean pair and were left devastated after failing to convert despite matching the top seeds for most of the contest.
Heartbreak
“We were very sad because there were a lot of chances. It wasn’t just one chance,” Manav said.
“Before the match, we had the belief that we could win. We played well and our decisions were good, but somehow they were better than us.”
Since then, the pair has made significant progress on the international circuit, climbing to World No. 2 before slipping to No. 3 heading into the continental extravaganza.
Manav, however, was wary of letting expectations become a burden.
“It is a very big opportunity. Last time, we missed out on a medal and this time we are No. 3 in the world, so expectations are there,” he said.
“We hope to give our best and win a medal for the country. But at the same time, we are enjoying every match and the process.”
Keeping it simple
For Manush, the immediate priority remains simpler.
“I always feel the next match is the priority,” he said.
“We are enjoying the training and the process. Results are not something we can rely upon, but enjoying the process is something that is constant.”
Manav and Manush will hope they can finally redeem themselves.

briefs.headline: Mona Agarwal secures LA 2028 Paralympic quota with silver at World Championships
briefs.deck: Mona Agarwal has secured a spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics after clinching a silver medal at the WSPS World Championships in South Korea. With a score of 250.0 points, she finished just behind the gold medalist. This accomplishment not only marks her inaugural World Championships medal but also serves as a pivotal moment in her journey, as she sets her sights on winning gold in 2028.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Indian para-shooter 
Mona Agarwal
 secured a quota place for the 2028 Paralympic Games in Los Angeles after winning silver in the women’s 10m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event at the WSPS World Championships in Changwon, South Korea, on Thursday.
The 38-year-old finished with a score of 250.0, just 0.2 points behind Serbia’s 22-year-old Kristina Trifunovic, who claimed gold with 250.2. The top two finishers were eligible for the coveted Paralympic quota places, meaning Agarwal’s silver earned India its first quota in the event.
For Agarwal, the achievement also marked her maiden World Championships medal. She had previously won silver in the same event at the Changwon World Cup last year.
From missing quota by 0.3 to securing LA place
The quota was particularly meaningful for Agarwal because of her experience at the 2023 World Championships, when she narrowly missed out on qualification.
“Last time in 2023 when I had participated in the World Championships, I missed the quota by 0.3. It was my second international match and I was very nervous,” Agarwal told RevSportz.
“I still have those memories fresh in my mind. I participated this time with all those learnings and I am happy that I could achieve whatever I wanted to. 
So, the performance this time and the medal means a lot to me,” she added.
Agarwal, who hails from Sikar in Rajasthan and was afflicted with polio as an infant, won a bronze medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games.
She recalled another memorable moment from her journey.
“I remember in March 2024 during the New Delhi World Cup, I was told that you have the last ‘bacha-hua’ quota. I considered even that as a glory but this time I am grateful to almighty that he supported me and I could secure the first quota place,” she said.
Avani wins bronze as India clinch team gold
Paris Paralympics gold-medallist 
Avani Lekhara
 also finished on the podium, taking bronze with 229.4. However, she could not secure a quota as only the top two finishers were eligible.
Agarwal and Lekhara combined to help India win the team gold medal in the event.
Agarwal already has her sights set on Los Angeles.
“In 2028, I want the medal colour to change into a Gold and I am also planning to secure a medal in the 50m event, since it would be my first achievement in 50m if I get one,” she said.
“In shooting and para-shooting, the quota place belongs to the country and not the individual athlete who secures it. The final list of participants is decided through trials and assessments closer to the Games.
